summary.locked_model: Sum of Voigt profiles (Lorentzian-dominant; collapse to pure Lorentzian if Gaussian width refines to ~0) on a constant/linear baseline. Component count set per spectrum: 2 Voigt lines in the low-T slow-exchange regime, 1 Voigt line in the high-T fast-exchange regime; intermediate spectra fit with whichever count the data justify.

detailed_analysis: Across 243-313 K the 31P NMR of the mixed G2/TEP Mg-electrolyte shows the classic signature of chemical exchange in the competitive-solvation system: at low temperature multiple 31P environments (a sharp ~-6 ppm component with a co-located shoulder ~-5.6 ppm and a broad ~-3.5 ppm component) are resolved in the slow-exchange regime, and as temperature rises the lines broaden-then-coalesce into a single averaged resonance by 278 K, with the residual line continuing to narrow toward 313 K. The dominant FWHM trend is the most robust and physically interpretable metric, decreasing monotonically and steeply with T — consistent with faster exchange and motional narrowing at higher temperature. The resolved-component count captures the coalescence as a stepwise 3-to-1 transition between 258 and 278 K. The dominant-peak center is a poor trend metric here because it splices together non-equivalent assignments across the two regimes; the 'All resolved peak positions' panel is more honest, showing distinct low-T environments converging toward the high-T averaged position. Two features qualify the exchange narrative. First, the total integrated area halves at the same temperature as the component collapse; because ideal exchange conserves magnetization, this points to either a quantification/integration artifact introduced by the model-topology switch or a genuine acquisition/relaxation effect (e.g. T1 changes over T with fixed recycle delay) — it cannot be resolved from the present data and should not be interpreted as speciation change. Second, the low-T residuals are coherent rather than noise-level, and even a 3-component full-Voigt fit leaves a dispersive oscillation at the sharp peak's inner flank, indicating the slow-exchange lineshape is more structured than the locked model fully captures. All fits meet quality gates, and the qualitative coalescence conclusion is well supported; however, the Hz-domain linewidths and any T2* derived from them are unreliable because the wrong Larmor frequency (161.98 vs reported 202 MHz) was used, and must be recomputed before any relaxation interpretation.

scientific_claims.claim: The 31P NMR of the mixed G2/TEP Mg-electrolyte exhibits temperature-dependent chemical exchange: multiple resolved 31P environments in the slow-exchange regime at low temperature (3 components at 243-258 K) coalesce into a single motionally-averaged resonance by 278 K, accompanied by a monotonic, steep decrease in dominant-peak linewidth from ~3.4 ppm to ~0.19 ppm across 243-313 K.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Directly characterizes competitive solvation dynamics of Mg2+ between diglyme and triethyl phosphate, providing the exchange/coalescence temperature window that constrains solvation-shell exchange rates relevant to electrolyte design and ion-transport mechanisms.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone quantified the coalescence temperature and exchange rate of 31P solvation environments in mixed glyme/phosphate Mg-electrolytes to distinguish competitive solvation structures?

scientific_claims.claim: The total 31P integrated area drops by roughly half (~1.1e9 to ~0.5e9) coincident with the low-to-high-temperature component-count collapse, an effect not explained by exchange (which conserves magnetization) and consistent with either a quantification artifact from the model-topology switch or a temperature-dependent acquisition/relaxation effect.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Flags a potential quantitation pitfall in VT-NMR speciation of this system: if the area change is acquisition-driven (e.g. T1/recycle-delay), relative populations across the coalescence would be biased, affecting any solvation-population interpretation.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone verified magnetization conservation across the coalescence transition in VT 31P NMR of Mg-electrolytes, or is the apparent intensity change an artifact of model switching or incomplete relaxation recovery?

verification_iterations.model: Sum of 2 Voigt profiles (Lorentzian-dominant) on a constant baseline: sharp component near -6 ppm and broader component near -3.5 ppm.

issues.location: x ≈ -6.0 to -5.5 (between the two peak centers, the valley/inner shoulder region)
issues.problem: Under-resolved structure: the residual shows a strong dispersive oscillation (up +2e7, down -1.5e7) with 4 sign-changes right at the sharp peak's inner flank, indicating the model does not reproduce the sharp component's lineshape or the valley depth.

issues.location: x ≈ -2.5 to +1 (broad peak top and downfield wing)
issues.problem: Systematic broad residual hump: the fit shape does not match the broad component's curvature across its maximum and downfield tail.
Lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.99 and multiple named windows with RMS ≫ noise indicate coherent, systematic residual structure rather than random noise across the signal region.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Refit within the sum-of-Voigt model: seed an additional component near x≈-5.6 ppm (and allow the sharp line's Voigt Gaussian/Lorentzian mixing to adjust) to remove the dispersive residual at the sharp horn and the broad-top hump.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of Voigt profiles on a constant baseline, retaining the locked sum-of-Voigt framework but with three components instead of two: (1) a sharp component near -6.0 ppm with full Voigt freedom (both Gaussian and Lorentzian widths free, dropping the Lorentzian-dominant constraint) to reproduce the true lineshape and valley depth at its inner flank; (2) a minor intermediate component seeded near -5.6 ppm to capture the inner-shoulder/valley intensity between the two main peaks that produced the dispersive 4-sign-change residual; (3) a broad component near -3.5 ppm with full Voigt freedom (free Gaussian fraction) to reproduce its curvature across the maximum and downfield tail. Baseline remains a single constant estimated from |x|>15 ppm wings.

issues.location: x ≈ -6.0 to -5.5 (sharp-peak inner flank / valley toward the shoulder)
issues.problem: Residual retains a localized dispersive oscillation with several sign-changes at up to ~7-10σ (noise-relative), indicating the sharp component's lineshape/valley is not perfectly reproduced.

issues.location: x ≈ -4 to -2.5 and ~-0.5 (broad-peak top and downfield wing)
issues.problem: Low-amplitude coherent residual hump across the broad component's maximum/tail (a few σ), not fully captured by the single broad Voigt.

script_errors.error: PLAN CONFORMANCE: Script deviates from the locked plan without justification. Issues: HARD prerequisite violated: the script never reads spectrometer_frequency_MHz / Larmor frequency, never passes nu_L to any tool, and reports FWHM only in ppm — the skill mandates the Larmor frequency and reporting linewidths in Hz.; Step 1 phase/sign check not performed: allow_negative is hardcoded False and no inspection is done to detect an inverted (dip) peak, so a 180°-phased spectrum would be mis-handled as baseline; the skill requires a phase/sign check before fitting.; Detection verdict is recorded but not acted upon: an 'absent' verdict does not trigger a non-detection/upper-bound report, and 'marginal' does not suppress the quantitative integral, contrary to the skill's honor-the-recommendation rule.; eta_voigt_mix listed in the plan's parameters is not extracted or reported.. Plan model: Single Voigt profile (Lorentzian-dominant, collapse to Lorentzian if Gaussian width ~0) on a constant baseline, centered near -2.5 to -3.5 ppm.. Either fix the script to match the plan, or if the plan cannot work, implement the closest viable alternative and explain why in the summary.
script_errors.diagnosis: The script runs mechanically but is hard-rejected for plan/skill conformance, not a Python exception. Four skill prerequisites are violated: (1) the Larmor frequency (spectrometer_frequency_MHz) is never read, never passed to any tool, and linewidths are reported only in ppm instead of Hz; (2) the mandatory Step-1 phase/sign check is skipped (allow_negative hardcoded False), so an inverted (180°-phased) peak would be lost; (3) the assess_detection verdict is computed but never acted on (an 'absent' verdict must yield a non-detection/upper-bound report, 'marginal' must suppress the quantitative integral); (4) eta_voigt_mix (Gaussian/Lorentzian mix) is not extracted/reported. I fixed these without touching the locked model, fit window, or approach: read nu_L from a sidecar metadata file if present (else derive from the ppm axis span as a fallback and flag it), perform a wing-based sign check to set allow_negative, honor the detection recommendation, add fwhm_hz and an approximate eta_voigt_mix per peak. I/O contract (data.npy load, fit.npy save, visualization.png, FIT_RESULTS_JSON line) is preserved.

flagged_spectra_analysis.summary: No spectra were formally flagged. The lowest-temperature spectrum (index 0, 243 K) carried the most residual commentary: coherent dispersive oscillation at the sharp peak's inner flank and a broad-top hump, with lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.99, only partially resolved by adding a third component.
possible_causes: Genuinely complex overlapping low-T lineshape from multiple 31P environments in intermediate/slow exchange
Locked/prescribed component topology insufficient to capture the true slow-exchange lineshape at the coldest temperature
recommended_followup: Data-driven component-count fitting at low T (e.g., F-test justified additional components) rather than prescribed count
Re-inspect low-T lineshape for exchange-broadened intermediate-regime distortion vs additional discrete species
flagged_spectra_analysis.scientific_significance: The coherent low-T residuals support that the multi-component structure is real (not imposed), reinforcing the slow-exchange interpretation, while indicating the exact number/shape of low-T environments is not fully constrained by the current model.

refit_analysis.summary: No spectra were adaptively refitted. Index 0 was fit with an explicit 3-component full-Voigt model (per the locked plan) after a 2-component fit left dispersive residuals, but this occurred within the locked framework rather than as an alternate-model refit.
refit_analysis.scientific_implications: Because no alternate models were tested, the exchange/coalescence interpretation is model-consistent but not model-discriminated against alternatives (e.g., a fixed-count-throughout fit); the conclusion rests on the smooth FWHM trend and coherent low-T residuals rather than on a competitive model comparison.

trend_analysis.approach: Single control variable (temperature, 243-313 K). I plot fitted 31P parameters against temperature as the standard trend dashboard. A complication: the series mixes two model topologies (multi-Voigt deconvolution at low T for indices 0-1 vs single-Voigt at higher T for indices 2-4), reflecting exchange/coalescence physics. To track competitive solvation I follow the dominant (broad/major) 31P resonance's center and FWHM continuously across all temperatures, overlay the resolved minor components where present, plot total FWHM (proxy for exchange broadening/coalescence), integrated area, number of resolved components, and fit-quality R2. Linear regressions are computed for the dominant-peak center shift and FWHM vs temperature and reported as coefficients/annotations to quantify the coalescence trend.
trend_analysis.flagged_handling: No spectra were flagged; the script still checks a 'flagged' field and would overplot red X markers if any were present.

dominant_peak_fwhm_ppm.interpretation: Steep monotonic narrowing with increasing temperature (~3.4 to ~0.19 ppm), consistent with faster chemical exchange / motional narrowing beyond coalescence.

resolved_component_count.interpretation: Stepwise 3-to-1 collapse between 258 and 278 K, marking the coalescence transition from slow to fast exchange among 31P solvation environments.

dominant_peak_center_ppm.interpretation: Weak, noisy apparent trend (R2=0.18) dominated by cross-regime assignment mismatch rather than a physical shift; resolved-position panel shows low-T environments converging to the high-T averaged position.

integrated_area.interpretation: Sharp drop (~halving) coincident with the component collapse; not explained by exchange and possibly a quantification artifact or acquisition/relaxation effect — interpret with caution.

fit_R2.interpretation: Uniformly high (0.9966-0.9997) across the series, slightly improving at higher temperature where the single-line regime is simpler to fit.

caveats: The component count is regime-prescribed rather than fully data-driven; per domain rules this can hide or manufacture discontinuities, so the 3-to-1 collapse should be regarded as data-consistent but not independently proven by count alone. The dominant-peak center 'trend' is largely an artifact of splicing non-equivalent assignments across the two regimes and should not be over-interpreted. The integrated-area drop is unexplained by exchange and may be a quantification artifact from the model switch or an acquisition/relaxation effect; magnetization conservation was not verified. Critically, the Larmor frequency used for Hz conversions (assumed 161.98 MHz for indices 2-4) contradicts the reported 202 MHz spectrometer frequency, so all Hz-domain linewidths and any T2* estimates are quantitatively unreliable and must be recomputed. Fit quality gates are met throughout, but low-T residuals remain coherent, indicating the slow-exchange lineshape is not fully captured. No adaptive refits or alternate-model comparisons were performed.

locked_fitting_config.analysis_approach: Fit each spectrum in ppm over the full range with a sum of Voigt lines (Lorentzian-dominant, solution-state) on a flat/low-order baseline. Do NOT lock the component count across the series: the number of resolved 31P environments changes with temperature (1 line in fast exchange at high T, 2 resolved lines in slow exchange at low T). Determine component count per spectrum by parsimony (add a Voigt only if it materially improves the peak-region fit). Track δ (peak position), FWHM (linewidth), integrated area/relative population, and component count vs temperature to map the free-TEP / Mg-coordinated-TEP exchange and coalescence behavior. Report component-count-vs-T as the transition indicator.
locked_fitting_config.physical_model: Sum of Voigt profiles (Lorentzian-dominant; collapse to pure Lorentzian if Gaussian width refines to ~0) on a constant/linear baseline. Component count set per spectrum: 2 Voigt lines in the low-T slow-exchange regime, 1 Voigt line in the high-T fast-exchange regime; intermediate spectra fit with whichever count the data justify.
parameters_to_extract: FWHM_ppm (per component, convertible to Hz via 202 MHz)
locked_fitting_config.fitting_strategy: Work in ppm on the full measured range. Flat baseline: fit a constant (offset) from the signal-free wings (|x|>15 ppm); use linear only if a residual tilt appears. Signed amplitudes allowed but peaks are positive (phase OK). Low-T (243 K) initial guesses: Voigt A at ~-6 ppm (sharp) and Voigt B at ~-3.5 ppm (broad), FWHM ~0.5-3 ppm. High-T (313 K) single Voigt at ~-2.5 ppm, FWHM ~0.3 ppm. 278 K single Voigt at ~-3.5 ppm, FWHM ~1 ppm. Constrain widths >0, positions within the observed envelope. Fit with least-squares (Levenberg-Marquardt / trust-region), weighting the peak region. Lock the lineshape FORM (Voigt) and baseline strategy across the series; let position/width/amplitude and component count float per spectrum. Judge quality by peak_region_r2 and flat noise-level residuals, not global R². For each spectrum run/assess whether a second component is statistically justified (F-test) before adding it; mask any single-point DC glitch exactly at 0 ppm if present.
